pick.thesis: Ranked first among today's eligible candidates on operating margin trend, growth acceleration, revenue growth, trailing year — revenue +738.8% over the trailing year, growth accelerating against the previous quarter, operating margin wider than a year ago, earnings fully backed by cash.

pick.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below -79.5%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $19.77 on the decision date.
risks: The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-09-30, 15 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-10-15.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-01-28) plus 364 days

pick.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
pick.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

sources.fundamentals: SEC Financial Statement Data Sets (twelve quarters), point-in-time by accepted timestamp, topped up from companyfacts for companies that have filed since the newest data set
sources.prices: Massive (Polygon.io) grouped daily bars, splits and dividends

stories.title: Rare pink diamond goes on display in France 100 years after amateur heist
stories.excerpt: The French royal jewel will be on public display for the first time since it was found hidden in an apple after a 1926 theft.
stories.lead:
A rare pink diamond is going on display in France for the first time since it was stolen almost 100 years ago to the day - the last time it was shown to the public.

The nine-carat, pear-shaped gemstone known as the "Grand Condé" was pilfered in an overnight raid on the Château de Chantilly in October 1926 and concealed in a hollowed-out apple.

The diamond - one of few royal jewels to survive the French Revolution - was recovered a few weeks later when a hungry maid at the hotel in which the thieves were staying took a bite of the apple.

stories.title: Decades after apartheid, South Africans seek justice for crimes of the past
stories.excerpt: More than three decades after the end of apartheid, families of victims of some of the worst crimes of South Africa's past are still fighting for justice. As survivors and perpetrators grow older, a new wave of legal efforts is seeking truth, accountability and reparations before it's too late.
stories.lead:
SHARPEVILLE, South Africa – Paulina Mathinye gestures with anguish at the rows of garbage-strewn graves, overrun with weeds, in the cemetery where her father is buried.

"Look at that, where they sleep," she says of the dozens of Black protesters buried here, all of whom were killed when police opened fire on March 21, 1960 in what became one of the bloodiest days in apartheid history.

"Why are they dirty? It's a disgrace," says the 71-year-old grandmother, who wears a floral dress and a smart sunhat.

stories.title: No Kings turns its focus to voting this weekend. Here's what we know
stories.excerpt: The coalition behind nationwide anti-Trump protests is shifting its strategies this weekend to focus on voter turnout. Organizers say Saturday's events are a nonpartisan effort to get people to the polls.
stories.lead:
No Kings, the coalition known for organizing anti-Trump protests, is trying a different democratic tactic: increasing voter turnout.

On Saturday, grassroot groups across the country will hold over 3,000 "No Kings: Vote Early" marches and other events. Organizers say these events are a nonpartisan effort to promote early voting in the midterm elections, and will involve helping people check their voter registration, make a plan to cast their ballot and understand their voting rights.

The voting push effort marks a pivot for the No Kings coalition, which comprises hundreds of partner organizations, including the American Civil Liberties Union and Black Voters Matter.

stories.title: Oregon teacher fought school attacker before armed dad shot suspect 'multiple times'
stories.excerpt: The 16-year-old suspect previously attended the primary school and had targeted a special educational needs classroom, police say.
stories.lead:
A female teacher in the US state of Oregon tackled a teenage shooter who entered her classroom and tried to wrestle the gun from his grasp, police have said.

The teacher, who has not been named, threw her mobile phone before trying to disarm the 16-year-old on the floor of a classroom at Silver Rail Elementary in the city of Bend.

The attacker killed three children and a teacher after shooting his way into the building on Thursday.

stories.title: Akerstrom Named Big West Player of the Week

A senior utility, Akerstrom led the 10th-ranked Tritons to a huge Big West road win at No. 7 Long Beach State last week. He racked up a season-high five points with four goals and an assist and tacked on a steal as well. His goal with 2:38 remaining in the game proved to be the game-winner against the Big West preseason favorite.

It was Akerstrom's third game back in action after sitting out since September of 2025 due to injury.

stories.title: Win Streak Hits Four for Men's Water Polo
stories.excerpt: Crimson down MIT to complete the weekend.
stories.lead:
CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- The Harvard men's water polo team won its fourth consecutive game with a 21-13 decision over MIT on the road in Cambridge. The Crimson improved to 7-10 overall and 4-1 in the NWPC, while the Engineers fell to 5-11 and 1-4.

Harvard led 4-2 after one, but MIT rallied in the second quarter and the Crimson's lead was just 7-6 at halftime. Harvard's offense ramped up the pressure in the third with three goals, led by two from senior Jacob Tsotadze, but the Engineers hung around with five goals of their own. Finally, the Crimson dominated the fourth with eight goals with two each from junior Dean Strauser and sophomore Emil Sogaard-Srikrishnan.
